item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
901
ABPZ20 KNHC 130531
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Sat Sep 12 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Norbert, located well west of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula.

Central and Western East Pacific (EP97):
An area of low pressure located several hundred miles southwest of
the southwestern coast of Mexico is producing disorganized showers
and thunderstorms, displaced to its south and east. Environmental
conditions remain conducive for development, and a tropical
depression is expected to form during the next couple of days while
it moves generally west-northwestward to westward over the central
and western portions of the eastern Pacific basin. For more
information, including gale warnings, please see the High Seas
Forecast issued by the National Weather Service.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...80 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Well Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
A broad area of low pressure located several hundred miles southeast
of Hilo, Hawaii, is producing minimal shower activity. Development
of this system is no longer expected.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...near 0 percent.

&&
High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service
can be found under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN02
KWBC, and on the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php

$$
Forecaster Adams

item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Sat Sep 12 2026 
341 
WTPZ34 KNHC 130848

BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Norbert Advisory Number  15
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
1100 PM HST Sat Sep 12 2026
 
...NORBERT STRENGTHENS SLIGHTLY...
...EXPECTED TO DISSIPATE WELL EAST OF HAWAII BY THE MIDDLE OF NEXT
WEEK...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 PM HST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...18.0N 131.7W
ABOUT 1450 MI...2330 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
ABOUT 1530 MI...2465 KM E OF HILO HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 280 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1000 MB...29.53 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM HST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Norbert was
located near latitude 18.0 North, longitude 131.7 West. Norbert is
moving toward the west near 12 mph (19 km/h), and this motion is
expected to continue during the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 50 mph (85 km/h) with higher gusts.
Some fluctuations in intensity remain possible over the next day or
so, followed by a gradual weakening trend.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80 miles (130 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1000 mb (29.53 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pierce/Gibbs

item.title: Tropical Storm Norbert Forecast Discussion Number 15
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Sat Sep 12 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 130849
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Storm Norbert Discussion Number  15
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
1100 PM HST Sat Sep 12 2026
 
Norbert's convective organization has improved during the past 
several hours. A renewed burst of deep convection, with cloud-top 
temperatures as cold as -80 C, has been expanding over the 
circulation. Recent ASCAT-A and ASCAT-B scatterometer passes showed 
an asymmetric wind field, with peak winds of around 45 kt north of 
the center. Given these new data and the improving convective 
presentation, the initial intensity is raised to 45 kt. 

The initial motion is estimated to be about 280/10 kt. The storm 
continues to be steered generally west-northwestward to westward 
south of a low- to mid-level subtropical that should persist through 
the forecast period. The track guidance remains in good agreement, 
although the latest guidance has continued to shift slightly 
northward. The updated NHC track forecast is largely unchanged, 
blending the previous advisory, the multi-model consensus (HCCA), 
and the Google DeepMind ensemble mean.
 
Little change in strength is expected during the next 24 h while 
Norbert remains in a marginal environment tempered by mid-level dry 
air and some west-southwesterly vertical wind shear. Some 
fluctuations in intensity are possible during this period as 
intermittent bursts of deep convection develop near the circulation. 
Thereafter, increasingly unfavorable conditions will induce a steady 
weakening trend. The NHC intensity forecast is largely an update of 
the previous advisory and shows Norbert degenerating into a 
post-tropical remnant low by 60 h and dissipating as it opens into a 
trough by 72 h. 
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  13/0900Z 18.0N 131.7W   45 KT  50 MPH
 12H  13/1800Z 18.3N 133.5W   45 KT  50 MPH
 24H  14/0600Z 18.8N 135.8W   45 KT  50 MPH
 36H  14/1800Z 19.1N 138.5W   40 KT  45 MPH
 48H  15/0600Z 19.4N 141.1W   35 KT  40 MPH
 60H  15/1800Z 19.5N 144.0W   30 KT  35 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 72H  16/0600Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Pierce/Gibbs
